column4: 在实际布展之前，我先用建模搭建了迷宫式的空间结构：路径怎样转折，框架和硫酸纸怎样分隔空间，观众在每个转角会看到什么。模型也标出了每个角度应该放置的绘画和装置，以及它们之间的位置关系。对我来说，空间本身就是作品的一部分。观众行走的路线，就是他们进入这段记忆的方式。
column5: This is a model I made of the whole exhibition space. Before setting up the place, I used it to plan the maze where the paths turn, how the frames and tracing paper split up the space, and what people see at each corner. The model also shows where each painting and piece goes, and how they sit next to each other. For me, space is part of the artwork. The path people walk is how they step into this memory.

column4: 从几个主要角度的作品现场图中可以看到，半透明的硫酸纸形成若隐若现的边界，绘画与装置分布在迷宫的各个节点。整体氛围安静、柔和，又带一点距离感。
column5: This page shows the installation from four main angles. You can see how the tracing paper  creates soft, half-hidden edges, and how the paintings and pieces are placed at different points in the maze. The mood is quiet and gentle, with a slight sense of distance. Before looking at each work up close, I hope this page gives you a feel for the whole space.

column4:
这个视角由一幅绘画和一件装置组成，表达的是我回忆中那些细碎、零散的片段。它们并不连贯，也没有清晰的开头和结尾，只是在某个瞬间突然浮现出来，又很快变得模糊。希望观众在这里
先感受到记忆的这种破碎感。
column5: This is where the first angle begins. It is made up of one painting and one installation piece, and it is about the small, scattered pieces of my memories. They don’t connect to each other, and they have no clear beginning or end. They just come up suddenly in a moment, then quickly fade. Here, I want viewers to first feel how broken and fragmented memory can be.

column4: 这幅画描绘了一个女性的背影，画面整体是模糊的，就像我记忆中母亲的样子。我的母亲本身就比较瘦，生病以后体重又严重下降。那段时间她非常痛苦，也非常希望自己能够重新长胖一点、逐渐恢复健康。我没有选择具体地描绘她的样貌，而是在模糊的画面中用线条去勾勒女性的身体。这些线条既是身体的轮廓，也像是身体正在一点点变轻、变淡。通过这种方式，我想表达身体的脆弱，也想表达我对母亲那段经历的记忆：清楚地知道它发生过，却始终隔着一层朦胧的距离。
column5: This painting shows a woman from behind. The whole image is blurry, just like how my mother looks in my memory. My mother was already quite thin, and after she got sick, she lost a lot of weight. She was in a lot of pain during that time, and she really wished she could gain some weight back and slowly get better. I chose not to paint her face or features in detail. Instead, I used lines to trace a woman's body within the blur. The lines are the outline of the body, but they also look like the body is slowly becoming lighter and fainter. Through this, I want to show how fragile the body is, and how I remember what my mother went through: I know clearly that it happened, but it always feels far away, as if behind a soft haze.

column4: 这件装置同样和母亲的病有关。她在治疗期间输过很多液，所以我用百合花代表生命，用下面的水代表人维持生命所需的营养和药物。花被浸泡在液体中，一方面像是在被“供养”，依靠液体维持着自己的生命；另一方面，它也像是被我封存起来的记忆，被隔绝在时间之外，却依然保持着鲜活。百合的洁白和脆弱，也让我联想到母亲在病中的样子。
column5: This installation is also connected to my mother’s illness. During her treatment she received a great deal of intravenous fluid, so I use lilies to represent life, and the liquid beneath them to represent the nutrients and medicine a person needs to stay alive. Submerged in the liquid, the flowers seem on one hand to be “sustained,” kept alive by what flows into them. On the other hand, they are like memories I have sealed away, held apart from time yet still vivid. The whiteness and fragility of the lilies also remind me of how my mother looked during her illness.

column4: 第二个角度由两件装置组成，主题是时间的流逝，以及那些被我们小心保护起来的记忆。随着时间推移，很多记忆已经不再像以前那样清晰，细节在慢慢消失，但事情本身并没有被忘记。我们依然记得它们发生过，也依然会在某些时刻想起它们。这个角度想表达的，正是这种“模糊却仍被保存着”的状态。
column5: The second perspective consists of two installations and is about the passing of time and the memories we carefully protect. As time goes on, many memories are no longer as clear as they once were, and their details slowly fade, yet the events themselves are not forgotten. We still remember that they happened, and at certain moments they still come back to us. This perspective sets out to express that state of being blurred yet still preserved.

column4: 在这件装置中，我使用了百叶窗，并把我小时候的照片作为影像投射在上面。百叶窗的叶片把完整的画面切割成一条一条的碎片，观众从不同角度看过去，看到的内容也不一样。有时能拼出一张完整的脸，有时只剩下断断续续的光影。这正是我对童年记忆的感受：零碎、模糊，好像记得，又好像不记得。百叶窗本身也是一种“遮挡”和“透出”并存的物件，就像记忆既在保护过去，也在隔开过去。
column5: In this installation, I use window blinds and project photographs from my childhood onto them. The slats cut the whole image into strips, so viewers see something different depending on where they stand. Sometimes a complete face comes together; sometimes only broken fragments of light and shadow remain. This is exactly how my childhood memories feel to me: fragmented and hazy, as if I remember, and yet I don’t. Blinds are also objects that conceal and reveal at the same time, just as memory both protects the past and holds it at a distance.

column4: 这件装置使用了计时器。它提醒我们时间始终在流逝。我想用它表达那些已经回不去的过去无论我们多么想停留在某个时刻，时间都会把我们一直往前推。放在这个角度中，它与旁边模糊的童年影像形成对照，一边是被留住的画面，一边是不断流走的时间。
column5: This installation uses a timer, a reminder that time never stops moving. Through it, I want to speak about a past we can never return to however much we wish to stay in a certain moment, time keeps pushing us forward. Within this perspective, it stands in contrast to the blurred childhood images beside it. On one side are images that have been held onto; on the other, time that keeps slipping away.

column4: 第三个角度更加温暖，也更加私人。我在这里想表达的是我记忆中母亲的形象，以及我和她之间共同拥有的回忆。相比前面关于病痛和时间的部分，这里更多是关于陪伴、关于日常，以及那些让我感到被爱的瞬间。
column5: The third perspective is warmer and more personal. Here I want to express the image of my mother as I remember her, and the memories she and I share. Compared with the earlier sections on illness and time, this part is more about companionship, everyday life, and the moments that made me feel loved.

column4: 这两幅小画表达的是小时候母亲对我的陪伴和呵护。在我的印象里，她总是很有耐心，会陪在我身边，一点一点地教我做很多事情。我选择用尺幅较小的画来表现这些内容，因为这些记忆是安静、细微、贴近身体的，需要观众走近、停下来，才能慢慢看清。
column5: These two small paintings are about the care and companionship my mother gave me when I was a child. As I remember her, she was always patient. She stayed by my side and taught me many things, little by little. I chose a small format for these works because the memories are quiet, subtle, and close to the body. Viewers have to come closer and pause before they can slowly make them out.

column4: 与两幅小画形成对比的，是放在地面上的一幅大画。它想表达的是记忆并不是完整的。过去的那些回忆，现在留给我的更多只是一种模糊的感觉。把画放在地面上，观众需要低头去看，甚至绕着它走动，这让观看变得像是在“寻找”什么。画面中的形象层层重叠、边界不清，就像我想努力回忆起什么，却始终只能看到一个大概的轮廓。
column5: In contrast to the two small paintings, a large painting lies on the floor. It speaks to the idea that memory is never complete. What those past memories leave me with now is mostly a vague feeling. Because the painting is on the floor, viewers have to look down at it, and even walk around it, so looking becomes a kind of searching. The forms in the painting overlap layer upon layer, their edges blurred. It is like trying hard to remember something and only ever seeing a rough outline.

column4: 紧挨着地面上大画的是一件行为作品。我写下了一个对我来说记得比较清楚的故事小时候，学校让我们种植物，我拿着种子回到家，和母亲一起把花种了下去。在大部分记忆都已经模糊的情况下，这是少数仍然清晰的片段。
column5: Right next to this large painting is a performance piece. In it, I wrote down a story I remember fairly clearly. When I was a child, our school asked us to grow plants. I took the seeds home, and my mother and I planted the flowers together. When most of my memories have already blurred, this is one of the few fragments that is still clear.

column4: 第四个角度表达的是我记忆中比较痛苦的一段时间。在这里，我使用药物作为材料，因为在我关于母亲的记忆里，药物占了非常大的一部分。它们代表着治疗和希望，同时也代表着漫长的病痛和无力感。
column5: The fourth perspective is about a more painful period in my memory. Here I use medicine as a material, because medicine takes up a very large part of my memories of my mother. It stands for treatment and hope, but also for a long illness and a sense of helplessness.

column4: 这件装置是把药物一颗一颗贴在墙面上。母亲生病期间服用了大量的药物，比如抗生素、止痛药等等。很多药物会带来副作用，而为了缓解这些副作用，又需要服用更多、更大剂量的药，形成了一个恶性循环。这个过程让我记忆非常深刻。当这些药物密密麻麻地排列在墙上时，它们不再只是药，而是那段日子的重量，也是母亲身体所承受的一切。我希望观众站在这面墙前时，能感受到这种重复、压迫，以及其中的沉默。
column5: For this installation, I attached pills to the wall one by one. During her illness, my mother took a huge amount of medication, including antibiotics and painkillers. Many of these drugs had side effects, and relieving those side effects meant taking even more medication at higher doses. It became a vicious cycle, and that process left a deep mark on me. Once the pills are densely arranged across the wall, they are no longer just medicine. They become the weight of those days, and everything my mother’s body endured. When viewers stand in front of this wall, I hope they can feel the repetition, the pressure, and the silence within it.

column4: 这件作品是从上一件延伸出来的，直接加入了输液的元素。在我小的时候，母亲需要注射药物，而我会帮忙，把药液慢慢推进她的身体里。这个动作在我的记忆中格外清晰，因为它很缓慢，也很小心。在这件装置里，我把花比作身体和生命，把水比作药物和维持生命的营养。液体一点一点流向花朵，就像当年那些药液一点一点进入母亲的身体。这件作品对我来说既是对那段经历的记录，也是一种重新面对它的方式。
column5: This work grew out of the previous one and brings in the element of intravenous infusion directly. When I was little, my mother needed injections, and I would help slowly pushing the medicine into her body. That gesture stays especially clear in my memory because it was so slow and so careful. In this installation, the flowers stand for the body and for life, and the water stands for the medicine and nutrients that keep life going. The liquid flows toward the flowers bit by bit, just as the medicine once entered my mother’s body bit by bit. For me, this work is both a record of that experience and a way of facing it again.

column4:
在整件作品中，我并不只是想讲述一个清晰、完整的故事，而是想营造一个感官性的回忆场域。迷宫般的路径、半透明的硫酸纸、柔和的光线，以及分布在各个角落的花、影像、计时器和药物，共同构成了一段非线性的记
忆。观众在行走、观看与停留中，会一点一点触碰到那些关于母亲、关于时间、关于被保存与被遗忘的片段。也许每个人看到的都不完全一样，就像记忆本身，从来不会以同一种方式被想起。
column5: With this work as a whole, I am not trying to tell a clear, complete story. Instead, I want to create a sensory space of remembrance. The maze-like paths, the translucent tracing paper, the soft light, and the flowers, images, timer, and medicine placed in different corners together form a non-linear memory. As viewers walk, look, and linger, they gradually come into contact with fragments about my mother, about time, and about what is preserved and what is forgotten. Perhaps no two people see quite the same thing, just as a memory itself is never recalled in the same way twice.
